patterns: how many bones are in the human hand
entries.answer: The human hand has 27 bones, divided between the wrist, the palm and five fingers, which is why it is unusually flexible for its weight. The thumb alone has three joints and its own set of muscles that let it oppose the other fingers, which is what makes a true grip possible. Most of the movement comes from forearm muscles whose tendons run through the wrist, so hand injuries can come from somewhere that looks nowhere near the hand. Carpal tunnel syndrome, a compression of the nerve in the wrist, is one of the most common hand complaints.

patterns: why do my eyes get tired from screens
entries.answer: The human eye focuses light onto the retina through the cornea and the lens, and adjusts for distance by changing the shape of the lens, a process called accommodation. The fovea, a dense patch of receptors in the centre of the retina, has no rods at all and gives sharp colour vision in daylight, which is why reading in dim light is hard. Eyes need regular blinking to stay wet, and screens reduce blink rate, which is a large part of why they cause dryness. The most common causes of avoidable sight loss are untreated cataract, glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy, all treatable when caught early.

patterns: how many fingers does a hand have
entries.answer: A finger is one of the five digits on a hand, and English names most of them individually rather than numbering them, which is not how the hand works anatomically. The thumb is the exception: it has only two phalanges while the other fingers have three, and it rotates across the palm rather than sitting in line with them. That opposition is what gives a hand its grip, so losing thumb function costs more than losing a finger does. The naming also differs by register, where ring finger and third finger are the same digit.

patterns: how many bones are in the body
why do babies have more bones
entries.answer: A bone is rigid tissue that supports the body, protects organs and stores minerals, and an adult skeleton has 206 of them, down from about 270 in a newborn as some fuse together. It is structural and chemical at once, holding calcium and phosphorus the body can draw on, which is why bone health is discussed alongside nutrition. Bone is living tissue that is continually rebuilt, and what a scan shows is the balance between the two rates rather than a fixed structure.

patterns: how many types of muscle are there
entries.answer: A muscle is tissue that contracts to produce movement, and the body has several kinds that do not all do that job. Skeletal muscle moves bones and is under conscious control, smooth muscle moves food through the gut and is not, and cardiac muscle pumps blood and cannot stop. Skeletal muscle is the one people mean when they say muscle, and the common misconception is that it builds simply by being used, when it builds by being used against resistance.

entries.answer: The knee is the joint that bends the leg, and it is the largest and most heavily loaded joint in the body, carrying several times body weight when climbing stairs. It works as a hinge rather than a ball joint, which is why sideways movement is restricted, and it is held together by ligaments and cartilage rather than by bone meeting bone directly. Pain in it is commonly caused by something other than the joint itself, since the tendon below the kneecap and the meniscus are the usual suspects.

patterns: how many bones are in the foot
entries.answer: A foot is the structure that bears the body's weight and absorbs the shock of each step, and it contains a quarter of all the bones in the body, which is why foot complaints are so specific. The arch is the key feature: it is what lets the foot roll rather than land flat, and flat foot is a loss of that arch. Feet change shape across a lifetime, and most adults carry some degree of pronation, which is why fitting matters more in older people than in children.

patterns: how many layers does skin have
why does a cut on the hand hurt more
entries.answer: Skin is the body's largest organ, covering several square metres and forming a barrier against water loss, infection and physical damage. It has two main layers, an outer surface that continually replaces itself and a deeper layer carrying the blood vessels and nerves. That nerve density is why a cut on the hand is far more painful than one on the back, since the same skin is more densely supplied in some places than others. It also does substantial immune work, because the surface is where most invading organisms first meet the body.

patterns: how fast does the heart beat
entries.answer: The heart is a muscular pump driving blood around the body, and it beats several billion times over an average lifetime without ever resting. Its four chambers separate the two circuits, with the right side sending blood to the lungs and the left sending it everywhere else, which is why a heart attack is a left-side problem. It is about the size of a fist and it beats from before birth, so its sound can be heard earlier in development than almost anything else.

patterns: how much energy does the brain use
entries.answer: The brain is the control centre for the body, and it is roughly two per cent of body weight while consuming about twenty per cent of the body's energy. That imbalance is the central fact about it, since it cannot store fuel the way a muscle can and depends on a constant supply of glucose and oxygen. It is also divided into regions with different jobs, so damage to a small area can remove one narrow function while everything else appears normal.
